figures.caption: Figure 1. Historical evidence has conflict-dependent behavioral utility. a, PPC suppression, PUL suppression and TRNto-PUL activation were tested in separate mouse cohorts. b, The workflow shows sensory history from the five preceding trials, the 500-ms intertrial intervention and the subsequent judgment. Regular trials use unequal tone counts. History probes pair equal counts with the source-defined catch flag. The post hoc logistic model estimates the intervention-related change in history weighting. c, Laser-minus-control differences in current and history accuracy for PPC (nine mice), PUL (ten) and TRN-to-PUL (six). d, Additional intervention benefit under history–stimulus conflict relative to agreement. Open circles show individual mice and diamonds show cohort means. e, History-by-intervention coefficients for the base model, after adjustment for prior intervention exposure and behavior, and after further adjustment for session drift. Bars show 95% mouse-bootstrap intervals. Extended Data Figures 1-1, 1-2 and 1-3 show intervention schedules, fitted behavioral contributions and evidence-strength comparisons, respectively. The brain illustration uses Allen Institute for Brain Science Mouse Common Coordinate Framework surfaces (CCF 2017, structures 997, 22, 218 and 262). The mouse head is adapted from Alexandra Rother (2024), SciDraw, doi:10.5281/zenodo.11431268 (CC BY 4.0).

Figure 2. Returning source content reconstructs history from identical network states. a, Two histories generate intact PUL feedback records in the same fixed circuit. At replay onset, both recipients start from the arithmetic mean of the complete 500-dimensional states. One second of own, pair-mean or opposite PUL input replaces the arrival at PPC through the original trained projection. Endogenous feedback then resumes under shared fifth and sixth stimuli. b, Native output half-contrast 𝐻𝑡 = (𝑦+ 𝑡 − 𝑦− 𝑡 )/2 in checkpoint G20, measured from replay onset. Bands identify replay and the current and later response windows. The natural reference follows intact trajectories. c, G20 separation of the rate vectors across all 500 units. Own and opposite replay overlap by paired symmetry, and the pair-mean control stays at zero. d, Later response-window contrast across nine checkpoints. Curves and points summarize 12 base histories crossed with two strong current stimuli. Shading in b and horizontal bars in d show 95% whole-base bootstrap intervals. Extended Data Figures 2-1 and 2-2 give the theory of reconstruction and compare the historical content carried by current amplitude and spatial pattern.

Figure 3. A substituted history survives a correct intervening judgment. a, Two intact recipients exchange PUL-toPPC messages for 1,000 ms after trial 4. In the illustrated G20 pair, both recipients make the same correct judgment on the shared strong fifth trial and then commit to opposite choices on the balanced sixth trial. b, Current and later sign accuracy under natural evolution, pair-mean replay and opposite replay. Trial 6 accuracy uses the original history target. c, Absolute changes in window-mean output between natural evolution and opposite replay, for the current and later responses. d, Later sign accuracy after PPC-only state averaging, comparing 500-ms pair-mean and own-source replay. e, Original, opposite and absent native commitments during trial 6 after 1,000-ms opposite replay. A commitment requires reaching the corresponding threshold (±0.75) without reaching the opposite threshold during the response window. Markers link the fixed checkpoints in b–d. Each condition uses 48 base histories crossed with four strong fifth stimuli and both history signs. Extended Data Figure 3-1 shows current choices across stimulus mixtures.

Figure 4. Source organization connects low-dimensional history to attainable messages. a, The paired PUL rates share mean 𝜇𝑇 and differ by 𝑑𝑇 . A candidate difference 𝑑′ 𝑇 keeps each of 70 source rates in [0, 20] and reaches 400 PPC units through the original projection 𝐵. b, Source-difference energy captured by the leading direction in 12 fitting histories and 12 independently sampled test bases per checkpoint. c, Fraction of tested time/context points reaching the natural receiving-current norm within 1%. Complete clipped-path matching uses the first target crossing or the largest attainable norm. Blue diamonds show the learned axis and open circles show three fixed random axes. d, Source transformations in 48 fresh bases per checkpoint, crossed with four strong fifth stimuli and both history signs. The plots show relative displacement of receiving current (left), loss of later historical contrast relative to own replay (center), and temporal roughness relative to the natural message on a logarithmic axis (right). Maps preserve the paired source mean, source bounds, receiving-difference energy and native E/I aggregate differences. The 64- and 256-proposal maps share an ordered candidate sequence. The smoothed map averages changes over five updates and restores receiving energy. Horizontal bars show paired 95% whole-base intervals for historical loss. Extended Data Figures 4-1 and 4-2 separate current magnitude from direction. Figures 4-3 and 4-4 compare boundedsource reallocation with direct tests of arrival-current direction. Figures 4-5 and 4-6 show temporally coherent reallocation and the geometry of clipped source axes.

Figure 5. Functional sensitivity at target and source levels. a, Target-current redistribution preserves the paired mean, the differential sum and energy within each native excitatory or inhibitory recipient class, and nonnegative arrivals. b, Boundedsource transformations act on 70 PUL rates through the original projection to 400 PPC units. Both assays replace one second of input after full-state pair averaging. c, The four plots, from left to right, show historical loss averaged over four target-current maps (24 base histories), historical loss under three bounded-source transformations, signed sensory-output change, and native current commitment. The source plots use the same independent sample of 48 base histories crossed with four strong fifth stimuli. Historical loss is the own-replay contrast minus the transformed contrast. Horizontal bars show paired 95% wholebase intervals, and shading marks the predefined ±0.02 native-output-unit range. Circles, squares and diamonds distinguish the 64-proposal, 256-proposal and smoothed maps in the source plots. Extended Data Figures 5-1, 5-2 and 5-3 show the geometry of target reallocation, its effects on choices, and the source-map sensory responses at each stimulus strength.

Figure 6. Retained differences, receiver thresholds and recurrent propagation shape historical use. a,b, Activitydifference RMS norm and RMS alignment with the fixed readout during current and later responses, respectively, after 500-ms own-source replay from intact states. Links pair response windows within each checkpoint (16 bases crossed with four strong stimuli). The alignment axis is logarithmic. c, Baseline fractions of absolute PPC readout contribution from linear pairs and pairs crossing the lower or upper rate threshold. Small points show checkpoints and large points with connecting lines show checkpoint means. d, Changes in later historical contrast under a calibrated inward common-state shift and the mean of eight fixed equal-norm directions. e, Changes following 100-ms partial attenuation of recurrent-drive difference. f, Signed current sensory-output changes for the inward shift and attenuation under strong negative and strong positive stimuli. Shading marks the predefined ±0.02 range. Panels c–f use 48 independent test bases per checkpoint, with doses in d–f selected on 12 separate calibration bases. Bars in d–f show paired 95% whole-base intervals. Extended Data Figures 6-1 and 6-2 illustrate saturation and decompose historical readout. Figures 6-3 and 6-4 show the effects of larger receiver perturbations. Figure 6-5 shows dose calibration and responses to the smaller perturbations.

Figure 7. Current evidence shapes historical expression and conditional receiver propagation. a,b, Historical halfcontrast across current evidence strengths at trial 5 and at trial 6 after a fixed strong-negative trial 5, respectively. Natural histories and 500-ms opposite-source replay are compared in 12 paired bases per checkpoint. Thin curves show checkpoint means and thick curves show their average. c, Mean observed (solid) and predicted (dashed) G20 paired output differences over 90 updates after the pip train, colored by evidence strength. d, The left plot compares held-out trajectory RMSE for evidence-specific gains with recurrence, pre-sensory gains with recurrence, the same evidence-specific gains with leak alone, and an independent reference-response template. The center plot gives template-minus-gain mean squared error with paired 95% whole-base intervals. Positive values favor gain propagation and negative values favor the template. The right plot shows within-evidence 𝑅2 for evidence-specific gain propagation with the within-evidence observation mean as baseline. Panels c and d use 12 reference histories and 24 independent test bases. Propagation models start from each test trajectory’s measured initial state difference. The template uses the evidence-specific mean response from the reference histories. Extended Data Figures 7-1, 7-2 and 7-3 compare retained state separation, history across evidence and trial positions, and alternative trajectory forecasts, respectively.
